text: A passer-by photographed the front of Jens Hofer's house on Elm Street while walking past in the morning.
The same man photographed Jens Hofer's house on Elm Street again, on a second day, from the opposite pavement.
From a grey Volkswagen with covered plates parked on Maple Road, a person filmed the entrances of the Community Centre for over an hour through a telephoto lens, face hidden by a hood.
An anonymous account, user handle nfld_watch, posted in a local forum asking for the home address of Maria Klein, giving no reason.
A user shared a map marking the locations of the Community Centre, the Place of Worship and the Northfield Community School.
Karl Brandt, who has a history of hostile posts about Community X, wrote that the community would soon be made to pay.
Karl Brandt posted that he would hurt people at the Community Centre during the harvest festival on Saturday.
Karl Brandt purchased a shotgun from a licensed dealer in Northfield.
Brandt bought ten litres of accelerant and a printed street map of Maple Road on which the Community Centre was circled.
A poster calling himself Northfield Patriot asked for like-minded people to help him do something about Community X.
A man in a dark jacket timed how long it took to walk from the car park into the Community Centre and out again, and was seen noting the positions of the security cameras.
Maria Klein reported that the same grey Volkswagen was parked outside her home on Elm Street on three evenings, with the driver watching the house.
Someone posted a photo of the Place of Worship on Church Lane with a caption mocking the community.
A user compiled and shared a list of names and workplaces of members of Community X, including Maria Klein and Jens Hofer.
A person sketched the exterior layout of the Community Centre from a bench across Maple Road.
Someone posted a 3D fly-through model of the Community Centre interior reconstructed from publicly shared event photos.
An estate agent from Northfield Homes Ltd, wearing a company lanyard, photographed the front of a house on Elm Street that is listed for sale.
A tour group photographed the Place of Worship on Church Lane as an architectural landmark, led by a guide.
Anna Weiss, a journalist at the Northfield Gazette, asked members about their public roles for a bylined story on community life.
An art student from Northfield College sketched the Community Centre for a class assignment, with the assignment sheet visible.
A delivery driver in a marked ParcelGo van was parked outside Maria Klein's home on Elm Street on several days, delivering parcels.
Thomas Berg, a licensed hunter with no hostile history and no connection to Community X, bought a shotgun from a dealer in Northfield.
Community organizer Ruth Adler compiled a contact list of members for the harvest festival invitations.
A commentator criticised the leadership of Community X over a planning decision, in strong but non-violent terms.
A person photographed the sunset at Northfield Beach.
A shopper bought groceries at the Maple Road supermarket.
Two friends planned a birthday party over chat.
A commuter took the train from Northfield Central to the city.
A car was seen near the Community Centre.
Someone was asking about community members.
A concealed observer with a camera watched Maria Klein's home on Elm Street.
